newsitem.title: GERMANY: Police probe bomb threat to Berlin's Love Parade.
newsitem.headline: Police probe bomb threat to Berlin's Love Parade.

text.p: Police stormed the homes of 31 suspected neo-Nazis to probe an anonymous threat to blow up the Love Parade street party where a million ravers are expected to gather this weekend, Berlin officials said on Thursday.
Berlin justice ministry spokesman Ruediger Reiff said an anonymous letter to city interior minister Joerg Schoenbohm prompted the search.
The letter claimed three anti-tank mines would be laid at the parade if the event was not called off.
"Several pieces of writing and computer diskettes were confiscated during the searches, but we have found no evidence to suggest the threats against the Love Parade are serious," Reiff said.
The ninth annual Love Parade, dubbed the largest techno music party in the world, is to start on Saturday afternoon and draw visitors from across the world.
Techno, which arose from American disco music, features simple synthesiser riffs or repeated musical motifs driven by a pulsating beat.
Last year a gyrating mass of 750,000 techno fans descended on the city to dance down a six-km (four-mile) stretch of a central Berlin boulevard closed off for the event.

Right-wing extremists are hostile to the event, which this year runs under the motto of "Let the Sun Shine in Your Heart", because they say it attracts foreigners to the city and supports music that has "Americanised" German culture.

Environmentalists petitioned a Berlin court to ban the event, arguing it would cause huge damage to plants and trees in a park in the centre of Berlin which is a nature reserve. The court rejected their suit.
German anarchists have also registered their disapproval, calling the Love Parade a purely commercial ploy and many of plan counter-demonstrations to coincide with the giant rave.
A police spokesman said a peaceful weekend was expected in Berlin despite the threats.
